name: intro_body
text:
Microscopy reconstruction supports optical inspection when clearer boundaries also produce more stable position measurements. Objective changes alter object-space sampling, optical blur and the pixel phase of motion. The variation of measured single steps provides a direct test of reconstruction for displacement inspection.

MOSR reconstructs each monochrome image on its native pixel grid. One fixed set of learned weights serves 20× and 50× objectives. This study examines each objective at a common nominal step of 1 µm, with Raw, fixed Wiener and MOSR sharing the same image pairs and circle-center calculation.

text: Fig. 1. Raw and MOSR images from the 20× and 50×, 1 µm datasets. Each comparison uses the same field and grayscale range. Scale bars: 2 µm.
textPreview: Fig. 1. Raw and MOSR images from the 20× and 50×, 1 µm datasets. Each comparison uses the same field and grayscale range. Scale bars: 2 µm.

name: methods_body
text:
Reconstruction. MOSR combines U-Net context [1], anti-aliasing [2] and bounded PSF guidance. The optical inputs comprise 25 measured kernels at 20× and one calibrated kernel at 50×. Fixed Wiener uses a regularization value of 0.0565.

Localization. Coarse contours [3] initialize maximum-gradient boundary points. Geometric least-squares circle fitting [4] uses 64 points at 20× and 96 at 50×. Every pillar starts from the same fixed calculation state.

Displacement. The median of nine pillar-center changes defines each step along the acquisition motion direction. The 20× dataset contains 30 complete scans of 30 steps. The 50× dataset contains 30 locked adjacent-frame pairs.

name: conclusions_body
text:
At 20×, MOSR lowers pooled within-scan step variation by 52.3% and improves all 30 repeated scans. At 50×, Step SD falls by 23.5% for the fixed 1 µm condition.

One reconstruction model supports both objectives with their calibrated optical inputs. Clearer boundaries and reduced displacement variation support MOSR for cross-magnification optical inspection.

20x: September 3 thesis cohort, 30 complete scans, 30 observed adjacent steps each. The line chart shows each scan SD. Summary is pooled within-scan SD, sqrt(mean(scan SD squared)); scans contain equal counts. This is not an average across acquisition conditions.
50x: July 2 original 1 micrometer cohort, 30 Raw-locked adjacent pairs. The bar chart is one sample SD per method from those 30 steps.
These are separate acquisition cohorts, not a matched causal isolation of magnification. All three methods share identical inputs and the same native normal-gradient geometric LSC reader within each condition.
The 0.5 micrometer 50x condition is retained in the complete audit and supplementary results; the submitted manuscript is unchanged.
All measured source numbers, reconstruction checks and citations are in the independent experiment workspace. The submitted manuscript supplies references [1]-[4].
